observations: Photo 0: Black lens held in hand, front barrel shows focal length scale markings '12 15 17 20 24' and aperture scale, with 'SIGMA' nameplate and an AF/M switch on the side.
Photo 1: Front element of the lens shown with hood attached, no visible fungus or scratches in this angle, but lighting and resolution are limited.
Photo 2: Side/rear barrel shows a label reading 'LENS MADE IN JAPAN' and a serial number '1016378'. No lens mount, contacts, or rear glass element are visible in any photo.
No photo shows the rear mount plate, electronic contacts, or any Canon EF markings that would confirm the mount type.
No video or multi-angle shot of autofocus operation, aperture blade movement, or zoom ring action.
No shot of the rear optical element or a light-through test to check for fungus, haze, or scratches.

identity.model: 12-24mm (exact full model number, e.g. f/4.5-5.6 EX DG, not fully legible)

claims.claim: US used Sigma 12-24mm lens for Canon camera
claims.evidence: No mount, contacts, or Canon-specific markings are visible in any photo to confirm the mount type or origin claim.

claims.claim: The lens looks new and in perfect working condition
claims.evidence: No clear optical, mount, or functional (autofocus/aperture) test shots provided; only exterior barrel photos from a hand-held angle.

risks.risk: Lens mount may not be Canon EF as claimed, making it unusable for the buyer's camera.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the rear mount showing Canon EF bayonet and electronic contacts.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unknown/incompatible mount risk, treated as unusable until mount is confirmed

risks.risk: Internal or optical faults (fungus, haze, scratches, dust) not visible from exterior shots.
risks.proof: Photos of front and rear elements against a bright light source, and a close-up of the glass.
risks.if_unproven: priced as if optics are compromised (worst case)

risks.risk: Autofocus motor or aperture blades may not function despite cosmetic appearance.
risks.proof: A short video showing autofocus engaging and aperture blades stopping down when mounted on a camera.

risks.risk: Zoom/focus ring smoothness and possible internal rattle (common issue in this lens line) cannot be assessed remotely.
risks.proof: A video demonstrating smooth zoom and focus ring rotation without grinding or rattling sounds.
risks.if_unproven: priced as mechanically uncertain, treated as faulty until shown working

proof_requests: Clear photo of the rear mount showing lens contacts and mount type (Canon EF bayonet).
Video of the lens mounted on a Canon body showing autofocus and aperture operation.
Close-up photos of front and rear glass elements against light to check for fungus/haze/scratches.
Video of zoom and focus ring rotation to check smoothness and absence of internal rattle.
response.reason: The lens model is identifiable by type and brand, but no photo shows the mount, rear contacts, or any functional test, so even a worst-case price cannot be set without confirming Canon compatibility and basic function.
